name: Dato
tagline: Check your calendar, upcoming meetings, and world clocks without leaving the menu bar.
description:
Dato is a menu-bar calendar, clock, and time-zone utility for macOS. It keeps the current date, upcoming events, multiple clocks, and a compact calendar within a click or shortcut, which reduces the need to open a full calendar app just to orient around the day.

Use it to scan upcoming meetings, see another time zone before messaging someone, create or join a calendar event, and keep a more informative date-and-time display in the menu bar. It is designed for people who want calendar awareness to be ambient rather than a separate destination.

## Features

- Show a customizable date, time, and calendar in the macOS menu bar.
- View upcoming events and interact with supported calendar events from the menu-bar popover.
- Track multiple time zones for distributed work, travel, or family.
- Use keyboard shortcuts and quick access to reduce calendar context switching.

## Where it fits

Dato fits people who make frequent small calendar and time-zone decisions throughout the day. It is a companion to Apple Calendar, Fantastical, or another calendar system rather than a competing planning database.

It adds persistent menu-bar surface area, so it is best for users who value immediate scheduling context. A simple system clock may be sufficient for an uncomplicated schedule.

## Privacy and requirements

The current Dato release requires macOS 26 or later. It reads calendars and reminders through the sources already configured in macOS and displays local clock and time-zone information; access to those databases must be granted by the user. Joining meetings or running scripts can open external services, but Dato is not itself a replacement calendar account.

## Pricing

Dato costs $18 for a one-time license.
